This paper outlines a comprehensive theoretical framework for explaining the fracture toughness of solid crystals at their most basic level. By applying the principles of thermodynamics, it describes the behavior of dislocations within the solids as they relate to stress. Furthermore, it identifies the equilibrium state that reaches the lowest possible energy for these dislocations under fixed external stress. The research demonstrates that arrays of regular geometric form held together by surface bonds can achieve lower energy states than linear sequences and illustrates that these regular patterns develop naturally from the movement of dislocations towards one another. The research also explores how the solids might transition from perfect crystals with no dislocations to those with multiple dislocations. The theoretical findings are compared with existing models and theories as well as observations from real-world studies of fracture. The research specifically examines and explains the fracture toughness of solid crystals at their most resistant level to stress. The theoretical findings are compared with existing models and theories as well as observations from real-world studies of fracture.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops Gaussian free field-valued processes in the upper half-plane and the first orthant of the complex plane, establishing their connection to multiple SLE evolution. We demonstrate that these connections result in Gaussian free field-valued processes that include the Dyson model, the Doob--Lambert--Loewner--Kagan--Sinai model, and the Yang--Chen model, among others.

In this research, we address the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in multi-dimensional space with smooth periodic initial conditions and obtain analytical estimates of the solution's maximum norm, tied to the initial conditions' maximum norm.

The verification problem for quantum computation is crucial and challenging, where a quantum server attempts to convince a less computationally powerful classical client that a function computed was done so via a quantum process. Currently, the most efficient classical verification protocols for quantum servers that handle quadratic functions take O(poly(κ) |F|^{3/2}) time and require a poly(κ, n) pre-processing step. In this research, we develop a new protocol that verifies quadratic functions in the server's quantum circuit in O(|F|^2) time without any prior processing, which significantly improves on previous methods. Although this time complexity is higher than in some recent multi-server protocols, we also present results indicating that a single-server protocol like this one comes at a near-optimal cost in some circumstances.

A blockchain system enables secure interaction among parties with conflicting reliability, making it a prime candidate for establishing trust within the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, where its applications extend beyond digital currencies. In this context, we explore blockchain technology and its applications in IoT, focusing specifically on its capacity to address IoT-related challenges. A thorough understanding of the underlying blockchain technologies and their adaptability to IoT is crucial in identifying suitable solutions for trusted IoT environments. We discuss IoT-specific problems and the advantages of using blockchain solutions, while also highlighting existing limitations and potential future research directions.

Generating synthetic cell shapes realistically can contribute to developing training datasets to enhance cell tracking and segmentation capabilities in biomedical imaging. However, creating accurate and diverse synthetic cells that mimic real cells' complexity is a challenge due to their intricate nature. Representing cell shapes using voxel-based representations is simple but prone to errors when dealing with boundaries, while polygon meshes can produce accurate boundary curves but is complex to construct and prone to errors when reproducing the smooth boundaries of cell shapes. Level sets of signed distance functions (SDFs) provide an alternative, representing the cell shape boundary with greater accuracy and flexibility. SDFs enable the efficient representation of complex shapes with high precision and can be easily modified to reproduce real cell shape characteristics. Nevertheless, directly generating SDFs from real data is difficult, so we instead trained an autoencoder to convert voxel representations of synthetic cells into SDFs, which allowed us to utilize established cell shape synthesis techniques based on voxel representations. Our trained model demonstrated the capacity to generate various cell shapes with high accuracy by inverting real cell shape voxels. Additionally, we introduced a post-processing approach to correct the generated SDF boundaries, resulting in a ground truth-like accuracy. Our method successfully produced synthetic cell shapes with high precision in ground truth-like metrics, which surpassed previous approaches and closely resembled real cells. These synthetic cells were used to train an U-Net to improve real-world cell shape segmentation tasks. Our approach was applied to two datasets from nucleus and colon cells to produce synthetic shapes with high

Blind, low-vision, and other print-disabled individuals still struggle with printed documents. Our focus in this paper lies on developing a method to automatically convert ordinary documents into high-quality, readable digital formats, specifically designed for recent blindfolded blindfold devices. We introduce DOCC, a document information extraction model that leverages optical character recognition with the aid of pre-trained vision models to inferr the document's layout and content. By combining the extracted information with digital correction tools, DOCC can produce readable digital versions of the document, making it accessible to individuals with disabilities. Our results demonstrate DOCC's effectiveness on documents of varying types and formats, even surpassing human performance in correcting two digital document issues. We showcase DOCC's capabilities through a video showcasing its application of a page-turning simulation, where the document's layout is recognized and replaced with a high-quality, readable digital version, including page layout restoration.

While BERT excels at modeling bidirectional contexts through denoising autoencoding, its reliance on input masking overlooks positional dependencies, leading to inconsistent pretraining-finetune performance. This has motivated the development of XLNet, an enhanced pretraining approach based on autoregressive language modeling. This method enables bidirectional contextual learning by leveraging the capabilities of autoregressive models combined with BERT's masking objectives. Interestingly, XLNet outperforms BERT in multiple benchmarks and achieves state-of-the-art results on various text classification and machine translation tasks. Moreover, our approach to modeling autoregressive redescription networks proves effective for modeling bidirectional contextual dependencies.

We've conducted in-depth studies of the exoplanets K2-18 b, K2-18 b's counterpart in the Kepler-62 e system, and the hot Jupiter TDs L 98-44 b using the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Telescope. By analyzing near-infrared spectra of these planets during their transits, we've identified key features related to water vapor, methane, and carbon dioxide. Our analysis took into consideration the impact of stellar activity and modeled the observed data using a power-law distribution to estimate the stellar radius, planetary radius, and surface pressure. Our findings suggest that water signatures in the spectrum of K2-18 b may be affected by stellar activity, while data from the other two planets reveal decreasing signals at wavelengths around 7.7 micrometers. Our results for K2-18 b show a water abundance 1.2 to 4.4 times higher than previously estimated, with a stellar radius of 0.443 and 0.457 solar radii. For Kepler-62 e, we've detected features related to carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide, given the stellar system's favorable conditions for atmospheric characterization. Our analysis of L 98-44 b's data suggests a carbon-to-oxygen ratio significantly higher than in Jupiter's atmosphere.

We will explicitly construct conformally distinct metrics on Riemann surfaces that have a finite covering number with respect to a given base metric, and include non-Euclidean versions of the standard Euclidean and Lorenzian metrics. This construction will be based on a generalization of the He and Ye technique for conformally distinct metric computation, and applied to singularities on Riemann surfaces that can be mapped to a real line under conformal transformations. As a consequence, we will obtain many pairs of distinct metrics on Riemann surfaces, and in special cases, we will obtain surfaces with non-equivalent conformal structures that have a finite covering number with respect to a given base metric, and can be mapped to either a real plane or the de Sitter space of radius one.

Research into the swimming motion of the centipede forficatus near the surface of water-water interface shows it doesn't use its 14 leg pairs primarily for movement; instead of most aquatic animals that move by creating waves along the body, this species moves using waves in the opposite direction, from tail to head. Its low mass and the presence of fluids against its body cause movement dynamics where drag forces overcome inertia, which can be explained using theories initially based on microorganisms. These theories, it's found, can accurately describe the centipede's motion as well. Additionally, the research shows that to walk on the surface of water, the centipede must switch to using its leg pairs for movement.

The ultimate aim of this project is to design an efficient, high-performance computing model that attains the limits of current mathematical modeling for tsunami simulation. A significant outcome of this endeavor will be a comprehensive, open-access software model capable of generating accurate predictions for diverse scenarios of tsunami events. Differing from traditional models, our approach utilizes a dispersive model suitable for the rapid transmission of tsunami waves with short wavelengths. To validate the accuracy of our model, we compared the results obtained using the Shallow Water Equations with those from the widely-used approach introduced by Kanoglu et al. in 2008. Additionally, we have successfully tested the model's scalability on supercomputers, specifically the JUWEL cluster at FZJ with up to 2600 cores.

Recent observations from ALMA and Spitzer have uncovered a population of large, distant galaxies that are too faint to be seen in UV imaging taken by the Hubble Space Telescope. These galaxies, known as HST-dark, emit the majority of their light in the infrared spectrum at wavelengths between 1.5 and 5 microns. Research suggests that a combination of dust and space absorption hides the galaxies' UV light. To better comprehend these galaxies, we analyzed deep near-infrared and submillimeter images from NOIR and ALMA for a sample of large, distant galaxies, and then used spectral energy distribution fitting to analyze their properties. Our findings indicate that large, distant galaxies have stellar masses, mean stellar birth rates, and star formation rates per unit area significantly higher than those of local large, distant galaxies. They also have larger large-scale dust temperatures, higher large-scale dust mass density, larger large-scale dust radii, lower large-scale dust opacity, lower large-scale black hole masses, lower large-scale accretion rates, lower large-scale accretion rates relative to star formation, lower large-scale black hole accretion rates, lower large-scale large-scale bulge to disk ratios, lower large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large-scale large

We explore a theory of seven-dimensional gravity accompanied by a specific set of topological terms within the context of $SO(8)$-invariant general relativity. Our key achievement involves constructing static, spherically-symmetric black holes and soliton solutions that demonstrate gauge symmetry which persists even in the presence of a horizon. Furthermore, we find that the soliton solutions develop a smooth $SO(8)$-invariant metric as the gauge parameter approaches infinity, thereby establishing their stability. Building upon these black hole and soliton solutions, we then investigate the corresponding Euclidean real-time thermal properties using the AdS/CFT correspondence to obtain the thermodynamic properties of the dual gauge theory from which we can determine its free energy and a conductance scale. A detailed analysis of the thermal properties is also carried out across a broad range of gauge coupling values, revealing an intricate relationship between the gauge coupling parameter and temperature. Our study further encompasses an examination of three specific topological terms within this gravity theory and their respective differences in gauge coupling parameter dependence.

In a long and narrow container with horizontal axis, two types of disks with varying sizes and weights are placed in an alternating sequence. This container, similar to a channel, constrains the position of the disks even if they are freely moving. The study explores the jammed states achieved through long-term free evolution of the system, where multiple disks are allowed to escape and move freely within the container. The jammed states exhibit diverse characteristics depending on the size of the disks, their weight proportions, and the sequence in which they are placed. This system serves as an example to illustrate that, even with initial states having identical entropy, different jammed states can be attained, characterizing distinct macrostates that are mutually unreacheable. The study provides a comprehensive qualitative analysis of the jammed states, and in addition, it discusses both exact solutions and approximate numerical solutions to the problem.

Research suggests that future El Ni\~no events are likely to shift towards the Central Pacific variant, which has distinct implications for both regional and global climate conditions. To date, studies examining the impacts of East Pacific and Central Pacific El Ni\~no on rainfall have yielded mixed results, particularly when focusing on spatial and temporal scales. A comprehensive study, encompassing observations from 1981 to 2010 and driven by atmospheric conditions, aimed to evaluate the differences in precipitation patterns resulting from East Pacific and Central Pacific El Ni\~no events. A key aspect of this research involved dividing the Pacific into sub-regions to analyze the effects of each type of El Ni\~no event. A significant disparity in precipitation levels was observed during Central Pacific El Ni\~no events, particularly when comparing it to East Pacific El Ni\~no events. A notable consequence of this disparity was the observed reduction in precipitation in the eastern South America region during Central Pacific El Ni\~no events, coupled with increased precipitation in the central and eastern Pacific regions. A statistical analysis using correlation coefficients revealed that Central Pacific El Ni\~no events exhibited a weaker link to precipitation patterns in specific regions, including the central Pacific, when compared to East Pacific El Ni\~no events.

When materials that don't have a regular structure are subjected to mechanical pressure, the distortion they undergo may deviate from expected behavior, even within their elastic range. The extent of nonaffine behavior varies depending on the material's underlying microstructure and can be difficult to predict. To simplify the analysis, researchers often use approximations such as the effective medium and the cell model, but these methods don't always accurately capture the dynamic relationship between the material's nonaffine deformations and the local stress it experiences. To better understand this relationship, a team of researchers has developed a state-of-the-art dynamic continuum theory that characterizes the nonaffine deformations and their impact on the material's overall properties. By integrating this new approach with existing static theories, the researchers were able to derive a general, time-dependent relationship that explains how nonaffine deformations affect a material's macroscopic properties. To test this theory, the researchers applied it to two specific scenarios: amorphous elastic materials and glass. By using numerical simulations to validate the theory, the researchers found that it accurately predicted the results, even at later stages and under different conditions.

This research investigates a population model, factoring in the effects of age and environmental pollution, comprising a single population with distinct larval and adult stages. The model's dynamics are influenced by intra-species competition among larvae, limited by their carrying capacity, and inter-species relationships between adults and the environment, characterized by birth and death rates that vary with the adults' age and pollution levels. Furthermore, the adults' interactions with pollution lead to pollution accumulation with further detrimental consequences for the population, while the adults' interactions with each other lead to population growth volatility, which can result in the loss and restoration of populations. Through both linear analysis and numerical simulation, the model reveals the occurrence of limit cycles, chaotic behavior, and chaotic transitions to extinction, as well as the potential for adult populations to adapt to environmental toxins through mitigation and recovery, and the impact of larvae on these processes. Without pollution, the model exhibits stable, positive, and constant population growth trends. However, the introduction of pollution leads to population growth instability, resulting in the occurrence of Hopf and Bogdanov-Levina-Li bifurcations, and the potential for adult populations to become extinct.

The researchers achieve decidability for an infinitely large group of axiomatic extensions to the Full Lambek logic, specifically those with certain weakening and contraction properties. This achievement builds on a previous result regarding the contraction counterparts of these extensions, while the computational complexity was not determined for them. In this study, we introduce just the necessary concepts related to well-quasi-orderings that make the proofs understandable even for those unfamiliar with this topic, whereas the original proof relied on more advanced logic principles. Ultimately, we outline how the findings can lead to applications in the field of proof theory.

Hierarchical taxonomies have immense value in numerous applications, but their applicability is restricted by the costly and time-consuming process of manual construction. Current research aims to automatically create taxonomies from existing concept representations. Hyperbolic geometric spaces are well-suited for modeling hierarchical relationships, as they naturally capture various distance categories. We introduce an innovative framework that utilizes a mixed hyperbolic Poincaré graph to generate hierarchies from concept representation embeddings. This approach can adapt to diverse distance patterns and handle complex hierarchy structures. We evaluate our method on two datasets and achieve superior performance on two metrics in comparison to traditional Euclidean space hierarchies and other benchmark graph-based methods.

Our research focuses on enhancing the theoretical prediction of hydrogen-bonded dimer interaction dipole moments by expanding the ANO1 test set to include various hydrogen-bonded molecules with large dipole moments. These dipole moments are oriented along the intermolecular axis, allowing for more accurate predictions. The ANO1 benchmark dataset initially overlooked H-bonded dimers with large dipole moments, primarily focusing on water-water and ammonia-ammonia interactions. However, our updated dataset, ANO1-HBD, includes 107 high-quality ab initio interaction dipole moments, encompassing diverse hydrogen-bonded dimers with large dipole moments, such as those found in acetamide-acetamide, formamide-formate, and other similar combinations. The new ANO1-HBD dataset offers improved applicability for predicting interaction dipole moments in molecular simulations involving large dipole moments. The evaluation of density functional theory tunneling and the use of R2SCF methods demonstrate the updated dataset's utility. Moreover, our research highlights the importance of including zero-point effects from density functional theory in the prediction of molecular interaction dipole moments. The ANO1-HBD dataset is now available online, along with accompanying data, including interaction dipole moments from density functional theory, Hartree-Fock, and other methods, as well as dipole moment surfaces, allowing for improved predictions of molecular interaction dipole moments.

The modern industrial system is characterized by a complex network of interconnected units that form an integrated system. However, inconsistencies and imprecisions often arise from various sources such as field conditions and the subjectivity of human judgment. These uncertainties often lead to unforeseen consequences like transportation disruptions and inaccurate budget projections. To mitigate these issues, a dynamic fuzzy control model is proposed to manage complex industrial systems with uncertain parameters. By incorporating fuzzy logic to describe uncertainty and dynamic control to simulate system interactions, the model accounts for the adaptive nature of fuzzy sets and facilitates real-time decision-making. Additionally, the model enables simultaneous calculation of system states and optimal control inputs, thus simplifying complex problem-solving and reducing computational burdens. As a representative example, the model is applied to managing industrial production systems with uncertain parameters.

Cyber-Physical Systems require robust resilience properties to withstand and adapt to continuous disruptions in their environment, which affects their operating capabilities. Disjointness resiliency protocols are one approach that ensure system components remain functional even after failures, by isolating functioning units from faulty ones. However, resiliency schemes often overlook the physical nature of CPS, which our research aims to address by designing disjointness resiliency strategies for magic square mechanisms - a model representing distributed CPS systems. Magic square mechanisms combine probabilistic services with fault-tolerant mechanisms, allowing system components to operate concurrently while preventing information conflicts. Building upon existing resiliency schemes for magic square mechanisms, we propose new resiliency models, along with associated algorithms, which maintain a system's operational state despite failures. Moreover, our resiliency model for magic square mechanisms, characterized by a resiliency value, guarantees a specific system state after failures, which satisfies multiple operational requirements. A resiliency value of k ensures that a working unit remains at a safe distance from faulty components, which could cause information conflicts and component failures. When k equals the number of components, resiliency schemes effectively prevent information conflicts, which is a key requirement in magic square mechanisms. Using graph theory, we demonstrate that resiliency schemes for magic square mechanisms can be effectively created and maintained by managing walk lengths between faulty and functional components. A resiliency scheme with a given resiliency value k involves creating walks with a specified maximum length between faulty

One of the most pressing enigmas in modern physics is the existence of dark matter. Although it's confirmed that dark matter gravitationally affects luminous matter, this interaction makes accelerator-based searches for dark matter particularly challenging. This difficulty has prompted researchers to look for signs of dark matter at non-accelerator experiments that use anomalous magnetic moments and other sensitive parameters. This review synthesizes recent findings from experiments searching for dark matter candidates such as feebly interacting matter, neutral scalar particles, and light vector bosons, as well as axion-like particles, using a range of sensitive parameters including couplings to electrons, photons, and hadrons. The review presents comprehensive limits on these dark matter candidates in various parameter spaces.

Consider a complete, non-compact Riemannian manifold M with dimension m, equipped with a metric g that has lower and upper bounds. Let the manifold support a gradient Shrödinger information structure, with boundary conditions specified by a non-zero, smooth function f and a unique steady-state solution u of the heat equation, both defined within the manifold M. Under these conditions, we derive a formula for the gradient Shrödinger information structure, utilizing a local Laplace operator L_g and a point p in M. This formula expands upon previous studies, providing a precise expression for the gradient by subtracting and summing certain terms that converge uniformly to zero. One key term in this expression represents a multiple of the Laplacian of u applied to the position vector, a concept previously introduced by Wu-Yau. The other key term is a divergent expression, equivalent to zero outside of the manifold's boundary, and for points within this boundary, it can be reevaluated using a limit and a particular expansion of the Laplace operator L_g at the point p. The other terms within the expression are found to make no substantial contribution and can be ignored, given an appropriate choice of sample size.

Radio sources powered by an Active Galactic Nucleus, specifically core-dominated sources, exhibit polarization that follows the Inverse Faraday rotation measure (IFRM) phenomenon, which affects smaller angular sizes. Larger sources, however, exhibit more complex behaviors due to depolarization through turbulent medium interferences along the line of sight. This study aims to determine the dependency of polarization fraction on source size by analyzing the LoTSS dataset. After filtering 732 IFM sources, the results indicate a polarization fraction dependence on size. Sources smaller than 5 inches exhibit lower median polarization, at 0.18%, which increases to 0.32% for intermediate sizes and drops to 0.14% for larger sources. These findings align with depolarization expectations due to the depolarizing effects of depolarized large sources. These results can be used to correct polarization flux bias in IFM and narrowband polarimetry observations.

Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) are a type of mathematical model based on Markov processes, where an unobservable state transition sequence causes observable output signals to emerge. The probability distribution of these observable signals is determined by the state transition sequence, which can be predicted using the observable signals. HMMs consist of unobservable state sequences, state transitions, and local observation probabilities. The problem of inferring unobservable state sequences given an observation history is an important one, especially in HMMs. Variational HMMs provide a method for solving this inference problem, where an approximation of the true state sequence is found by minimizing the difference between predicted and actual output signals. We propose Hidden Markov Codes (HMCs), a new approach based on Variational HMMs, where the minimization problem is recast as a linear program. We demonstrate that under certain conditions, minimization of this linear program yields an exact solution, rather than an approximation. We also show that when the conditions are not met, the solution obtained is at most one standard deviation away from the optimal solution. We validate our approach using synthetic data, compare it with other methods for predicting state sequences in HMCs, and finally demonstrate the efficiency of our method by minimizing energy consumption in data centers.

We develop a class of stochastic advection problems to investigate turbulent transport properties, where the flow field statistics are represented as a continuous time Markov process. This representation accurately captures turbulence's essence, characterized by the shift from one coherent structure to another. Our analysis yields exact expressions for the turbulent transport coefficient and the diffusion coefficient of passive scalars, revealing their linear relationship. Our findings are validated through comparisons with direct numerical simulations of pseudo-transient two-dimensional turbulence.

We maintain that many 'good' fits to elastic scattering data are unwarranted,
lacking a complete understanding of the dynamics behind nucleon-nucleus and
nucleus-nucleus scattering. When phenomenological models fall short,
phenomenology often results in overfitting, although this can be rectified
by incorporating additional data. We suggest an alternative approach to
evaluating folding models in nuclear elastic scattering by utilizing a systematic
method to eliminate unnecessary complex factors. This involves comparing the
folding model to experimental results, using a systematic approach to
determine the necessary parameters and eliminate any unnecessary variables.
This improved methodology was applied to $\alpha$-$^{40}$Ca and $\alpha$-$^{48}$Ti
systems, utilizing a reliable set of experimental data, demonstrating that a
simple yet robust description of the interactions can adequately explain the
observed trends.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the electromagnetic radiation behavior in a thin conductor wall enclosure. Initially, the radiation's thermodynamic properties are examined through a thin slab, which the electromagnetic radiation can freely enter and leave. Upon applying the classical thermodynamic principles to this system, it's discovered that the radiation behaves as an ordinary gas. In contrast, when a magnetic field is introduced to a parallel slab configuration, it's found that the radiation's thermodynamic properties adhere to the principles of Landau quantization and the resulting de Haas-van Alphen effect. Consequently, an exotic gas behavior emerges, which is characterized by periodic transitions between gas-like behavior and a liquid-like state, all in response to varying temperatures and magnetic field intensities. Furthermore, the study also explores entropy changes in an adiabatic process and identifies a universal constant, much like $\gamma = \frac{5}{3}$ for ordinary gas.

Protecting users of location-based services with significant privacy requirements is extremely difficult when multiple locations are shared within a short time frame due to the significant overlap in their geographic areas. Current protection methods often come with significant service disruptions, making it impractical for users who frequently change locations. A new location protection approach called $k$-Anon $L^p$-Windshield has been developed to provide high-quality location-based services while maintaining users' privacy. This approach employs the generalized $k$-anonyme technique to protect the proximity of consecutive locations, where the proximity is calculated using the $L^p$ distance metric. Our approach minimizes service disruptions by only requiring minor alterations when consecutive locations share significant information. A new metric called privacy cost has been introduced to evaluate the effectiveness of location protection. Experimental results show that using the $L^p$ distance metric instead of the $k$-Anon method significantly reduces service disruptions and improves the quality of location-based services up to 300%. Additionally, implementing distance constraints does not substantially decrease the accuracy of location-based services, from 93% when distance constraints are absent to 91% when distance constraints are applied.

A crucial component for autonomous driving and a persisting challenge is place recognition, especially in environments with limited or no GPS coverage. We propose a novel, lightweight approach leveraging neural architecture search to develop effective repeatable detectors for robotics and autonomous vehicles, leveraging advantages of dense net designs. Traditional methods rely on costly trial-and-error approaches to find the ideal network architecture for a given task. We introduce a linear model to estimate network architecture performance and apply it to the repeatable detector problem, demonstrating computational efficiency and significant performance gains over state-of-the-art benchmarks and commonly used architectures. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/kekeTop/topos.

Research has shown that combining resting-state functional MRI data from multiple sites can potentially introduce systematic biases in connectivity research. In this study, we aimed to understand how data from multiple sites are affected by large-scale connectivity measures, particularly in the context of functional brain networks. To this end, we utilized data from the 1000Brains project and analyzed it through different network measures. Our results show that site-specific biases primarily manifest at lower frequency bands in the brain's functional brain networks. Furthermore, we used statistical tests to compare the networks of control subjects and individuals with schizophrenia, and found that regardless of whether data from a single site or combined data from multiple sites is used, the detection power of the statistical tests is similar. This suggests that site-specific biases do not impede the detection of network abnormalities associated with schizophrenia when data from multiple sites is combined across a diverse range of participants.

In a single-hop beeping network, stations interact via one-bit messages to form a distributed communication system. We explore the distributed computing domain's two core challenges, naming and counting issues, and our objective is to refine existing algorithms to reduce their energy usage and processing speed. Our key contribution is the development of efficient, randomized algorithms to resolve these problems in optimal O(n log n) time, where n represents the number of stations in the network. Notably, while randomized solutions are typically faster, they often rely on probabilistic success, and past research yielded algorithms with runtime complexities of O(n log^2 n) and O(n^2/3) time, respectively.

Recent advancements in Natural Language Processing (NLP) for code-mixed language text have experienced significant growth, driven primarily by the increasing presence of Indian language content on social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook. Given the rapid spread of Hindi-English code-mixing (HMEG) online, there's a pressing need for developing suitable word representations that capture the unique semantic nuances of this language pair, posing a challenge due to the limited availability of datasets and linguistic standardization. To overcome this obstacle, we've created a large dataset consisting of 263k word-tuples, along with their corresponding frequency and grammatical category information, making it an extensive multilingual resource. By leveraging this dataset, we've successfully created the first ever word embeddings specifically tailored to HMEG, utilizing the popular Word2Vec framework. Additionally, we've employed various evaluation metrics, such as similarity tests and sentiment analysis analysis with KonetNLP, to assess the quality and accuracy of these embeddings. Our study demonstrates that although current HMEG word embeddings still fall short of those developed for monolingual and bilingual languages, they have shown promising performance, setting a foundation for further improvements in the future.

Using a combination of density functional calculations and the linearized Migdal-Eliashberg equations with the functional derivative approach, we analyze how the density of states affects the behavior of H3S as a function of pressure between 150 and 200 GPa. Our results show that accounting for the variable density of states leads to a more accurate prediction of H3S's critical temperature at high pressures, with a 10% increase compared to previous calculations. This improvement is attributed to two distinct transitions in the density of states at 150 GPa, specifically at omega = 5 and 15 meV. These peaks correspond to specific phonon modes that drive superconductivity in H3S. Furthermore, we find that the critical temperature reaches a maximum at 160 GPa before decreasing at higher pressures, with the density of states playing a crucial role in this behavior. Specifically, we show that the variation in the density of states alone is sufficient to explain the decrease in Tc at pressures above 160 GPa.

This paper introduces an innovative technique to create spatial buffers for preventing collisions in dynamic environments. In comparison to traditional methods that integrate global map-based planners, this approach leverages online global planning with minimal assumptions about the environment or trajectory libraries. A dynamic occupancy grid is applied to estimate thresholds for buffer sizes, with proposed formulations for horizontal and vertical spacing that do not rely on localization or topological maps. An evaluation using actual flight data on diverse vehicles in various conditions demonstrates the efficacy of this method, outperforming previous approaches while facilitating online global planning and trajectory smoothing.

This paper outlines our approach to visual relocalization using a point cloud derived from processed image data, where the 3D surfel map and multi-channel color information facilitate fast and robust loop closure detection and pose estimation. A proposed neural network model enables the creation of a color surfel map, where each point is represented by a multi-channel descriptor, and this representation is shown to outperform existing methods. Moreover, our approach eliminates the need for depth information and reduces the computational cost associated with point feature matching, as it leverages multi-channel color information to match and localize points. We evaluated our method on multiple datasets and observed significant performance improvements, and the proposed framework is now publicly available on GitHub.

In the context of multiuser MIMO, the task of jointly selecting users and precoding can be reformulated as recovering a group-sparse signal from underdetermined equations. Building on this reformulation, the paper introduces an algorithm grounded in the group LASSO approach. Relative to the current best practices, the proposed method delivers substantial gains according to numerical assessments conducted under realistic conditions inspired by cellular networks.
We demonstrate that the rational function semifield of a tropical curve has an algebraic description as a fraction of trigonometric functions within the algebraic closure of the complex numbers.

This note primarily focuses on measuring the speed of a conditioned process approaching its quasi-stationary equilibrium under specific assumptions regarding its distribution. In reverse, we establish that a conditioned process converging uniformly to a self-conservative, ergodic Markov process also attains a distinct quasi-stationary equilibrium, which it approaches at an exponential rate. Furthermore, we establish a functional limit theorem describing the behavior of the conditioned process relative to this equilibrium. This research is substantiated through related examples and empirical analyses.

We've demonstrated that combining the 1-cocycle of a long knot's space with Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles through integration produces a specific Vassiliev invariant, having a precise order of three. This discovery builds on a preceding finding by the second listed author, proving that I(X) integrated over the Gramain 1-cycles generates the Casson invariant, a singular, nontrivial, and robust invariant of order two after accounting for scalar multiplication factors. Similarities can be drawn with a part of Mortier's research.

LiFeAs, a high-temperature superconductor below 18 K, exhibits distinct electronic properties near its Fermi level, displaying either hole or electron character. By using x-ray emission spectroscopy in a non-destructive manner, we can distinguish between these two types of electronic states. For the first time, we've used this technique to observe a change in the electron state in a high-temperature superconductor. Our data indicates that the electron state near the Fermi level is restored in LiFeAs when it transitions into its superconducting state, as shown within our experimental range above 14 K.

This research reviews a global analysis of Type-II two Higgs doublet models and considers how upcoming measurements of the SM-like and charged Higgs sectors will constrain the parameter space of these models. Assuming no tree-level coupling of the two Higgs doublet fields to additional light particles, the models' vacuum stability and unitarity are validated. Predictions for the masses and production cross-sections of the charged and SM-like Higgs particles are made based on two Higgs doublet model scenarios. A combination of theoretical estimates and experimental data is used to constrain the parameter space of these models. Specifically, future measurements from colliders such as FCC-ee and ILC will significantly limit the range of possible charged Higgs masses. Additionally, the model's predictions for its flavour-related parameters are such that they do not contradict existing experimental data at present levels of sensitivity. Future experiments at LHC will also significantly limit the range of possible charged Higgs masses.

We demonstrate through simulated molecular surface experiments that neuroevolutionary learning can independently design particles and temporal strategies for enhancing spontaneous assembly processes, based solely on the desired end product and operating conditions. This algorithm can optimize spatial configuration, composition, and size distribution by selecting the most suitable conditions for a system of particles to form a target structure. By contrast, conventional design techniques rely on prior knowledge of temporal strategies and often sacrifice operational adaptability. Our research highlights the potential for automated and flexible optimization of self-assembly systems, which could significantly enhance the development of computer-optimized nanotechnology.

Our research appears to suggest a dynamical-Higgs-phase outcome in a broad range of chiral gauge theories, particularly those that are strongly-coupled. In the context of this scenario, fundamental leptons might experience significant residual interactions. What's more, the framework presented here could also apply to other related theories, such as the Einstein-Chern-Simons-Higgs theory, potentially leading to new insights into quantum gravity and the nature of dark matter and neutrinos.

This study contributes towards addressing a long-standing question raised by Tsurumi in 2019: under what conditions does the stationary Navier-Stokes equation remain stable in high dimensions? Specifically, we investigate the relationship between input forces and resulting flows in dimension d. This investigation shows that the stationary Navier-Stokes equation becomes unstable when the input forces decrease slowly with spatial frequencies for certain dimensions and types of flows. Specifically, we prove that: when dimension d is three or greater and the input forces decrease slowly with a exponent between d/2 and 1 plus d/2, the stationary Navier-Stokes equation loses its stability. Conversely, when the input forces decrease slowly with a exponent greater than d/2, the stationary Navier-Stokes equation remains stable.

We are studying how heat is transferred through a material using spin and electronic properties in antiferromagnetic insulators with specific collinear arrangements of spins. By utilizing the spin wave approximation, we have developed an expression describing how heat flows and found that it is influenced by the magnitude of nonlinear magnon interactions, the level of unpaired electronic spin, and the temperature. At higher temperatures, we have determined the self-sustaining limit of heat transfer and developed an expression describing how it changes with frequency. Our research reveals that the spin wave method can result in an inaccurate calculation of thermal conductivity, particularly at higher temperatures where nonlinear effects on magnon polarization become significant, and thus we recommend combining this method with a different approach for accurate results.

This research introduces two modifications for enhancing the security of Loidreau's code-based cryptosystem.
Originally built using Gabidulin codes within the McEliece framework, Loidreau's system is now vulnerable due to a potential key recovery attack.
We initially show how this attack can be applied to generic rank metric based code-based cryptosystems.
Next, we develop two modifications to overcome this vulnerability: the first involves incorporating a high rate low density parity check encodings to increase the computational difficulty of key recovery, and the second involves using a specific family of codes derived from linear complementary codes that offer inherent resistance to key recovery via rank metric attacks. We test the effectiveness of our proposed systems using moderate parameter sets and find that they maintain both computational efficiency and code uniformity at reasonable levels.

To improve pre-trained language models (PLMs), which dominate current state-of-the-art natural language processing performance, we need to overcome their limitations in handling language that is less commonly encountered, such as idiomatic expressions and colloquialisms. Research has shown that multi-lingual pre-training can mitigate this issue to some extent. However, this method has its own problems, including difficulty in effectively utilizing relevant sentences that are already familiar to the model. As a result, we propose a new pre-training approach that helps PLMs become more familiar with sentences that are less common but still convey more information. Our approach involves utilizing a large amount of unannotated text and a weak signal from an external knowledge base to identify and learn idiomatic expressions and colloquialisms using three different objectives. Our experiments using multiple datasets demonstrate that this method can lead to significant improvements over existing models and even match or surpass performance of models fine-tuned with expensive and targeted supervision.

The minimum weight spanning tree in graphs and its higher-dimensional equivalent, the minimum spanning acycle in simplicial complexes, were previously linked to a particular value by the zeta function. The zeta function helps us understand the behavior of these structures in terms of their weight distribution. Specifically, we investigated the behavior of weights in a particular type of simplicial structure called an acyclic flag complex with a finite number of elements. The results show that the weight distribution converges to a specific value as the number of elements increases. The study also considers situations where only partial data is available and finds that the weight distribution still converges to the same value. The study further relates this to the concept of non-normality in two-dimensional structures and shows that the weight distribution can be used as a measure of non-normality. The study also connects this to the behavior of a particular type of random walk on graphs, showing that the weight distribution can be used as a limit of the walk's steps.

This paper presents FedTwin, an innovative variation of horizontal federated learning. Unlike traditional horizontal FL, which combines data sets and training, FedTwin allows for the integration and simultaneous training of data sets and models based on client-specific objectives and constraints. The method accommodates both client-side data verticality and heterogeneity in training objectives, functioning alongside established FL frameworks. The proposed approach yields improved model symmetry, enhanced sample diversity, and increased training efficiency. Empirical evaluations on three research challenges, including multi-task learning, domain adaptation, and adversarial learning, demonstrate the efficacy of FedTwin in producing transferable models, outperforming the baseline models by significant margins.

A theoretical framework called B-Mesogenesis, which involves hypothetical dark matter components, predicts the existence of specific decays involving B mesons. Researchers investigated whether these predicted decays could be observed at existing particle colliders by simulating various experiments, such as proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. Assuming that the large scale of the underlying Lagrangian is beyond the scope of the theory, simulations indicated that while the decays may not be detectable at current facilities, more powerful facilities, such as those planned for the High-Luminosity LHC and the Future Circular Collider, may potentially reveal these decays.

In a Smart City environment with numerous agencies and interconnected cyber and social layers, safeguarding public safety is becoming increasingly complex. This growth in complexity makes it difficult for government agencies and the public sector to effectively respond to threats such as terrorist attacks and cyber attacks. As the world becomes smarter, the risk of failure in emergency situations also increases. Therefore, effective crisis management in these settings necessitates a collaborative effort among government agencies, the public sector, and the general populace. To facilitate this mission, various intelligent systems are being developed to provide real-time support to decision-makers and the general public during high-risk events and emergencies. Specifically, this research investigates the impact of terrorist attacks on urban ecosystems and introduces a concept for situational awareness in emergency response missions. Furthermore, the study proposes a novel approach to interconnecting diverse data sources and decision-makers through the application of data-driven and web-based technologies. This research presents a specific model for situational awareness, tailored to urban warfare scenarios. It also showcases a practical web-based system designed to gather and process real-time data from multiple sources, including social media platforms. This decision support system enables users to create dynamic situational awareness displays and facilitates collaborative decision-making by interconnecting different users with the ability to share information and manage access to this information based on their respective roles and privileges.

Researchers studied the Schwarzschild and charged black holes' behavior in an expanded universe model.  They considered these black holes within a larger space model where volume is included in the energy equation, alongside other thermodynamic properties.  Using the Hawking mass and entropy formulas, investigators derived the black holes' first law and stability, ultimately finding that the phase transition temperature is directly tied to pressure and a constant called kappa.  They discovered that the phase transition temperature is influenced by the universe's volume, but not its electric potential.  A graph illustrating the universe's thermodynamic behavior was produced based on these findings.  They examined the impact of the universe's volume on thermodynamic properties and phase transition temperatures, concluding that the universe's size affects its thermodynamic behavior.

Long document retrieval has been a longstanding challenge in both human comprehension and machine reading. While significant progress has been made by leading models in extracting relevant information from lengthy documents, the task becomes increasingly more difficult with longer documents and less coherent or redundant text. In this study, we introduce the Long Document Retrieval dataset which targets long document comprehension, establish a baseline approach using the Retrieve-and-FEw approach, and observe a notable performance decline with increasing document length. Notably, our results indicate that the Retrieve-and-FEw approach achieves scores 6-12% lower on average compared to the model's performance in standard RE reasons. Additionally, we explore two potential strategies to enhance the model's performance in long document comprehension: leveraging explicit length cues and augmenting the retrieval space, which show promising results in improving the model's performance and mitigating the effect of document length. Our code and dataset are publicly available.

Despite the impressive performance of Graph Neural Networks in semi-supervised node classification tasks, they face significant challenges when dealing with an extremely limited number of labels.  To address this issue, we've developed an innovative labeling framework that leverages local label distribution information to improve pseudo-label accuracy, combining this with a graph augmentation technique that utilizes pseudo-label information to refine node classification.  This method employs an enhanced loss function that utilizes both pseudo-labels and Ensembled GNN predictions to improve model training efficiency.  Our experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves performance on par with full-labeled ensembles for minimal-labeled scenarios, and significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods by a substantial margin.

This research exploits the unique properties of betatron radiation to analyze the plasma wakefield acceleration experiment EA-06 using the Lanzhou Microtron's electron beam. Through an accurate simulation of the plasma wakefield, the initial conditions of a witness electron bunch were determined and compared to measurements from an X-ray spectrometer. This led to the identification of two distinct phases in the plasma wakefield acceleration process. Furthermore, the analysis via betatron radiation spectroscopy revealed details about the plasma and the witness electron bunch that could not be obtained directly. As a non-invasive observation method, betatron radiation spectroscopy offers a promising approach for diagnosing high-energy plasma wakefield acceleration experiments.

This study introduces the first fully verified methods for privately learning decision trees in a hierarchical manner within a distributed framework. The proposed algorithm utilizes the differential privacy definition developed by Gupta, et al. in a previous study and further expands upon their work by offering alternative methods, each accompanied by tighter privacy bounds and performance analysis. The new approaches modify and enhance a data distribution strategy known as "MAD-WOOD" and aim to improve its efficiency. The research highlights significant trade-offs between efficiency and the amount of data required for accurate results, ultimately showing that our algorithm results in data reduction proportions that are exponentially better than the original distribution strategy. The study's findings also provide a general framework that can be applied to other distributed privacy preservation techniques for decision trees.

We address the task of regret optimization for a learner making sequential $k$-round decisions in the presence of observations drawn from a possibly non-i.i.d. population distribution. By establishing an information-geometric connection between Bregman divergences and Kullback-Leibert divergences, we propose a comprehensive optimization framework capable of being initialized at any starting point. By leveraging this framework, we develop an optimization technique with a reduced regret of $\sqrt{2k} \cdot \widetilde{O}(\sigma^2)$, where $\sigma^2$ represents the average second moments of the distribution. This method is versatile, applicable to various starting points, and specifically allows for faster convergence when initialized near a distribution close to the true one. By allowing the learner to adaptively choose its starting point, we significantly reduce regret, achieving a sublinear $\widetilde{O}(\log k)$ regret. Furthermore, in the context of online linear bandits, we present a dual averaging strategy with improved performance and flexibility when observations are $\alpha$-concave.

This generalises the discrete Bayesian network class to the chain event graph class, retaining the Bayesian network's benefits for interrogation, propagation, and learning, but allowing for more intricate modelling of temporal and sequential relationships among events. This paper explores the sampling and statistical learning methods for this expanded network class, specifically focusing on its probabilistic equivalent, the chain scotched graph, for efficient inference and parameter estimation. It also demonstrates that, on sparse datasets, the expanded network class excels the generalised Bayesian network class in terms of model selection and estimation. Finally, it highlights potential applications across multiple domains and encourages broader adoption of chain event graphs in practical modelling tasks.

Infinite-dimensional convex minimization problems, such as those arising from inverse problems or optimal control, are examined where the objective is to minimize a regularized value function over an infinite-dimensional domain within an infinite-dimensional output space. The value function is defined as the limit of a sequence of continuously differentiable functions that increase monotonically due to the problem's characteristics. The convergence to this limit is handled through Tikhononv regularization in an Karush-Kuhn-Tucker form, with the analysis focusing on deriving necessary conditions for the optimized value. The results are applied to a boundary layer optimal control issue where the boundary is approached asymptotically. The conditions derived are initially formulated for the optimized value to be finite before extending the results to consider the optimized value approaching infinity. The analysis of the infinite-dimensional problem is facilitated through a compactness argument that relies on the convergence of finite approximations towards an optimized value. The method employs Lagrange multipliers to translate the infinite-dimensional problem into an optimized value problem of a finite-dimensional dual, with the optimized value converging towards infinity towards a finite limit. The resulting dual problem is defined within an infinite-dimensional space of measures, with the analysis focusing on deriving necessary conditions for the optimized value by leveraging the properties of this space. The results are applied to a series of model problems, including boundary layer optimal control, hyperbolic systems, and elliptic inverse problems, with the necessary conditions for the optimized value derived in each case. The convergence towards an optimized value

This research investigates how basic autonomous entities similar to Braitenberg vehicles can demonstrate complex movements, navigating around static objects in their environment. Their dynamics are explained using a Lagrangian framework, which is then applied to scenarios in two and three dimensions. This theoretical approach reveals that simple, expandable bodies can exhibit a wide range of motions, including oscillating, rotating, and linear or angular movements in two and three dimensions, as well as a unique linear movement in specific two-dimensional configurations. Furthermore, our analysis shows that these agents can cover the entire range of possible configurations in their respective environments, implying that their dynamics is generally underdetermined. Extending this work, we explore the dynamics of three-dimensional agents with two and four degrees of freedom and find that their movements can be controlled by up to four external sources. Theoretical models are substantiated through simulations, which accurately replicate the predicted behaviors.

Within the framework of a kinetic energy driven superconducting mechanism, the effect of impurities on the transport of quasiparticles in cuprate superconductors in the superconducting state has been investigated, employing the nodal approximation. Results indicate an inverted shape in the microwave conductivity spectrum as it varies with energy, displaying a peak in the conductivity at intermediate temperatures, which declines with further increases in temperature. Notably, the microwave conductivity exhibits a reversal compared to the optimal doping regime, peaking at under and over doped states and plummeting around optimal doping, instead.

This passage discusses an anisotropic curvature flow, referred to as a crystalline curvature flow. A comprehensive review of this type of flow is provided, focusing primarily on the initial value problem. Key aspects covered include proving the existence and uniqueness of solutions, preventing blow-up, and confirming that the solution describes a smooth, moving plane in space.

Our survival relies heavily on plants, and they're uniquely adapted to thrive in nearly any condition. In any given season or location, plants modify their stem growth rates in response to the surroundings. Capturing this kind of dynamic change in a simple model proves to be a bit challenging. A straightforward approach, known as the Logan's equation, exhibits limited flexibility and doesn't accurately represent the observed variations in stem growth. On the other hand, a more advanced model, consisting of a nonlinear ordinary differential equation, effectively mirrors the changes in stem length over time. However, this new model proves to be difficult to analyze directly, prompting us to explore approximate solutions using the adhesive perturbations theory. By combining the model and approximate solution for small changes in stem growth, we're able to create a straightforward, easy-to-use formula that accurately predicts stem length for relatively small adjustments in the environment. In practical terms, this new formula works well for small changes in stem growth of up to 100 percent. In cases of more substantial changes, our model proves to be a reliable prediction tool.

It has been established that the SLE loop measure arises as a normalizing constant for conformal welding of LQG disks. This study explores multi-fingered conformal weldings as critical developments from multiple SLE loops. First, it proves that the conformal type of the resulting LQG surfaces converges in probability. Then, focusing on the scenario of two disks, it proves that the resulting surfaces converge to a single copy of the driving function's trace. This fills a gap in the proof of the Glimm--Schofield theorem for random surfaces.

The Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative is a global partnership that strives for consistency in extracting biomarkers from imaging data to enable efficient quantitative analysis. One significant hurdle in this field is the lack of standardization, which causes difficulties in reproducing and comparing results. To address this issue, IBSI has established guidelines for conducting and presenting research, including guidelines specific to applying computational image analysis techniques. Our study demonstrates the application of IBSI standards to a complex image analysis task, namely identifying macrophages in lung tissue images from patients with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, where the images contain varied features such as uniform patterns and background noise. By applying this standard, researchers can ensure that image analysis results are accurate and feasible to reproduce, thereby enhancing the validity of their findings.

We have analyzed the effects of high-spin nucleon and delta resonances on kaon photoproduction. Two covariant isobar models were employed to simulate this process, with the models being compared to experimental data. The models were also used to investigate certain features such as resonance structure and cross section behavior. The incorporation of high-spin resonances significantly improved the models' agreement with experimental data and reduced discrepancies associated with resonance structure. This inclusion resulted in notable model improvements. The models were further tested under off-shell conditions for nucleons and deltas, with the results showing little change. The models were applied up to photon energies of 3 GeV.

This research describes the process of preparing the MORPH-II dataset comprising 55,134 images. The methodology section delves into the individual steps of the pre-processing sequence, with section two offering a comprehensive overview of these stages. Section three provides detailed descriptions and calculations using OpenCV functionalities to illustrate each step in the pipeline, ultimately concluding with a retrospective evaluation of potential enhancements.

Building upon our previous research \cite{Liu:2019xhn}, we investigate how cogenesis relates to non-supersymmetric primordial black holes, keeping the black hole and baryon masses aligned throughout the collapse process. With the current observational constraints on black holes in the 10^18-10^22 gram range in mind, we examine the cogenesis parameter space and find that various theoretical models, such as inflation and particle creation during inflation, can accommodate primordial black holes making up all or a portion of dark matter within specific ranges of the cogenesis parameter. These regions of the cogenesis parameter space fall outside the exclusion limits from X-ray observations. Moreover, we demonstrate that certain scenarios, like black holes and baryons coalescing at the pre-inflationary stage, can satisfy the baryon and dark matter density requirements simultaneously. These findings expand our previous research to include scenarios outside the supersymmetric framework.

University administrators and educational researchers are concerned with understanding enrollment patterns at a large scale but often rely on decisions made without a solid analytical foundation. To address this, we developed a method for making course enrollment recommendations at a university with a large student body. Our proposed approach utilizes historical enrollment data and identifies key factors influencing student course enrollment based on decision theory. By considering the correlation between enrollment decisions, we established a probabilistic model for predicting future enrollments. The results show that this approach surpasses existing baseline methods and offers a flexible framework for making robust and informed enrollment recommendations.

This research examines the feasibility of enabling multiple connected and automated vehicles to form a closely-moving "platoon." An initial framework is developed to control the vehicles within this platoon using two primary information networks: a wireless communication system and a direct, high-speed data transfer method. Our analysis involves deriving mathematical equations that describe the movement of each vehicle within the platoon, assuming that the vehicles follow a straight route and are capable of exchanging data through the two mentioned systems. An optimal control strategy is then developed to minimize the overall distance between vehicles within the platoon, based on this mathematical model. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, simulations are conducted using real-world data, including varying speeds and distances between vehicles, and the results demonstrate significant improvements in minimizing the overall distance within the platoon under both data transfer methods. Furthermore, we show that the proposed strategy can maintain a safe following distance even in scenarios where the preceding vehicle accelerates rapidly, such as during a sudden upsurge in speed.

One of the most widely-used optimization method in machine learning is Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). When applying SGD to large-scale deep learning problems, the algorithm's performance is often limited by data transfer times due to the need to send gradients to multiple machines. Utilizing multiple machines in parallel can significantly decrease computation times but is ineffective when using traditional SGD due to the need to wait for each computation to finish before proceeding. Our novel approach, the Communication-Avoiding SGD (CA-SGD) method, is designed to minimize the communication of data by averaging gradients locally and only sending the final averaged gradients at the end of the iteration. This allows local averaging to occur simultaneously with the computation of gradients, ultimately resulting in reduced overall computation time. Our experiments using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets with up to 128 machines demonstrate CA-SGD to be 2.1 to 2.3 times faster than traditional SGD and 1.6 to 2.1 times faster than Stradivarius, the leading parallel SGD method.

The widespread dissemination of misinformation through the internet and social media significantly impacts public perception and user behavior, with generative models now making it quicker and cheaper to produce fake content. To safeguard against misinforming users and safeguarding our online communities, we must develop an effective detection system to identify the credibility of generated information, particularly in news headlines. Our study employs deep learning models on news headlines to distinguish between human-written and computer-generated, employing state-of-the-art pre-trained language models such as BART and XLM-R as the foundation for these models. By pre-training these models on vast multilingual text datasets, we can avoid the scarcity of data for specific detection tasks. The results of our cross-validation and ensemble method reveal impressive accuracy, reaching up to 89.3% across all models.

In polycrystalline, amorphous, and ion-damaged Kitaev materials, we demonstrate
that a spontaneous chiral spin liquid develops due to broken inversion symmetry.
Our conclusions are supported by detailed X-ray diffraction, neutron scattering,
magnetic resonance, and electron spin resonance experiments and density functional
theory calculations on specific samples. Our research in Kitaev materials paves the
way for creating chiral spin liquids through inversion symmetry breaking in
topological surfaces and opens up new avenues for producing and studying chiral
topological spin liquids through controlled crystalline transformation and ion
irradiation.

Future large-scale radio interferometers, aiming to detect 21\,cm signals across vast distances, may struggle with computing cross-correlations given traditional architectures, where the computational demand increases exponentially with the number of antennas involved. Traditional architectures, requiring the calculation of all antenna pairs, become impractical for arrays with many antennas. The introduction of the FFT-correlator architecture reduces the computational complexity, but its real-world implementation is limited by factors like data bandwidth and the need for real-time data processing. We investigated the feasibility of using the FFT-correlator architecture for the Square Kilometer Array, exploring its performance under realistic data characteristics and variability of antenna pairs. We found that the distinct spectral characteristics and dynamic volume of 21\,cm arrays might allow for more efficient implementation than previously thought, particularly if the spectral resolution is optimized to match the redshift distribution of the desired signals. By strategically choosing the spectral mode, it's possible to minimize the number of unnecessary antenna pairs, reducing the computational demand by half. We identified three distinct modes of operation, offering varying levels of complexity and a corresponding performance boost. These findings suggest that the FFT-correlator architecture can be adapted to suit the needs of 21\,cm arrays without extensive storage or data pre-processing.

For several decades, the Markowitz framework has been used for in-depth portfolio analysis but it places an excessive focus on understanding market uncertainty, failing to prioritize trend prediction. While researchers have applied generative adversarial networks and their variants to generate financial time series and assist in portfolio analysis, their approaches are also limited due to overemphasizing series generation at the expense of preserving future value predictions. This paper presents an innovative method to generate time series with trends that can help in both portfolio analysis and trend prediction, allowing for an effective integration of generative models and the Markowitz framework. The proposed model, called Trend-aware Conditional CGAN, leverages an extended input that includes past series values, which aids in capturing the time series trend. Experimental results on S\&P 100 and Shenzhen Component Index demonstrate the superiority of our approach over existing generative models in both Markowitz-based portfolio optimization and short-term trend prediction.

We have derived the polarized massive operator matrix element $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$
analytically to three-loop order in QCD for arbitrary values of $N$,
including both the limit where $N$ approaches infinity and specific cases of
lower $N$ values, like 2. This result was achieved using the expansion of Mellin
transforms and the solution to a $D$-matrix equation in hypergeometric terms.
Furthermore, our calculation contributes to the completion of the operator matrix
element spectrum at three-loop order. The resulting $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$ is
expressed in a mathematical representation suitable for further analysis or applied
to the calculation of the cross-section and its dispersion in the context of parton
distribution functions.

The multi-wavelength Blazar Catalog (BZCat) has around 440 Fermi-LAT blazar candidates, divided into the known, harder-spectra population, and a lesser understood softer population. Working with the BZCat's comprehensive list of candidates, our study aimed to classify all Fermi-LAT blazars into two categories, harder-spectra or softer-spectra types, to gain insights into the characteristics of each population. Utilizing the BZCat's detailed information and additional data from various sources, we were able to distinguish between the two populations of blazars. Our research identified 246 blazars with harder spectra and 194 with softer spectra, leaving the rest classified as uncertain due to insufficient data. These classifications are based on the full multi-wavelength spectral energy distributions, allowing us to identify blazars with double-component synchrotron-self-Compton emissions. The study also revealed 57 new blazar candidates with specific accretion disk properties. Our findings provide a comprehensive understanding of the two populations of blazars with harder and softer spectra, paving the way to investigating the evolution of Blazar populations with the complete BZCat dataset.

Active participation and content creation are key components of social networking, 
with users increasingly favoring short video and image-based content over text 
shared on microblogging platforms, enabling self-expression, social connections, 
and sharing news through personal stories and links to external websites. 
This study examines the trends in user-generated content on Chinese social 
networking platforms by analyzing official updates from eight popular sites, 
covering a period of 43 months and examining over 1.5 million posts for content 
types including text, images, videos, and links. Our analysis reveals the 
specificity of content preferences on distinct platforms, highlights the evolution 
of user-generated content, and sheds light on the correlations between 
macro-economical factors and short-term changes in this trend.

In our investigation of hypergraphs within the framework of the universal tensor cohomology theory, we demonstrate the tensor join property plays a pivotal role in capturing the essence of hypergraph structures. Utilizing the tensor join, a hypergraph can be broken down into a collection of minimal hypergraphs whose components in the tensor join decomposition coincide with their respective tensor join structures. By examining the properties of tensor joins in matroid and lattic hypergraphs, we derive new insights and findings, including characterizations of uniform matroid and lattic hypergraphs, a generalization of the basis exchange property, and proof that the tensor join structure of a pure lattic hypergraph is a pure subhypergraph. Additionally, we establish the existence of free hypergraph extensions for any given lattic hypergraph, and show that the tensor join of two free hypergraphs is also a free hypergraph. Furthermore, we apply the tensor join to derive new information regarding the passage from hypergraphs to their corresponding multi-linear structures, particularly in relation to Mnev's conjecture.

India achieved a groundbreaking success with the deployment and functioning of its initial space observatory, AstroSat, which marked a new era in space-based astronomical research (Sreekumar et al., 2015). Building upon this achievement, the country is preparing to launch two cutting-edge telescopes, the INdian Spectroscopic and Imaging Space Telescope (INSIST) and the Multiwavelength, high resolution, VLT Associate Telescope (MATHVS), which will deliver exceptional resolution and observational capabilities. These cutting-edge satellites will significantly advance our understanding of astrophysical phenomena in the following areas: determination of space-time geometry with an accuracy of $10^{-5}$ meters, investigation of the distribution of matter and energy across the universe with an accuracy of $10^{-13}$ grams per cubic meter, and detailed analysis of the formation and evolution of the universe through its observation of galaxies at various stages of development. This paper outlines the design and operational strategies of INSIST, which is scheduled for launch in 2022, and MATHVS slated for launch in 2023.
